examples.solution_text:
a) The marked $83^{\circ}$ angle is outside the shaded sector, so it is the exterior angle.

$\begin{aligned}\text{interior} &= 360^{\circ}-83^{\circ}\\&=277^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

b) The marked $277^{\circ}$ angle is outside the shaded sector, so it is the exterior angle.

$\begin{aligned}\text{interior} &=360^{\circ}-277^{\circ}\\&=83^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
A sector has an exterior angle of $231.5^{\circ}$.
Find its interior angle.

A sector has an exterior angle of $225^{\circ}$.
Find its interior angle.

methods.description: Subtract the given exterior angle from the full turn of 360 degrees to find the interior angle. Integer, decimal, minor and reflex results use the same method.
methods.sourceRef: booklets/mathsmap-sources/Stage 4/Area 2_Circles and Sectors.md lines 397–410, Identify Interior angle of a sector; lines 585–599, Development question 8

methods.description: Locate the marked angle relative to the sector's radii and bounding arc; explain when it is exterior rather than interior, then subtract from 360 degrees.

examples.derivation: a) The sector spans 83°–360°, so its interior angle is 360°−83°=277°. b) The sector spans 0°–83°; the marked exterior sweep is 277°, giving 360°−277°=83°. Both follow the identification activity at Area lines 397–410.
360°−231.5°=128.5°. The explicit exterior-angle wording supports subtraction directly; no diagram is necessary. Formatting preserves the original mathematics.
360°−225°=135°. This uses the source's full-turn relationship. Formatting preserves the original mathematics and the useful retained example.

The bounding arc spans 0°–110°, while the marked angle sweeps 110°–360° outside the sector: 250°. Therefore the interior angle is 360°−250°=110°. The explanation adapts Area lines 557–564 without introducing area calculations. Only the solution diagram labels the derived interior angle.
